test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 17 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A and B working together can do a piece of work in 3 days. B alone can do the same work in 12 days. How long (in days) will A alone take to do double the work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of 3 and 12 = 12 units.

Combined efficiency of (A + B) = 12 ÷ 3 = 4 units/day.

Efficiency of B = 12 ÷ 12 = 1 unit/day.

Efficiency of A = 4 − 1 = 3 units/day.

Time for A to do double work (24 units) = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A and B together = 3 days

Time taken by B alone = 12 days

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Total Work = LCM of given days

 **Days**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of A = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of B

⇒ Efficiency of A = 4 − 1 = 3 units/day

⇒ Total work to be done = Double of original work = 2 × 12 = 24 units

⇒ Time taken by A alone = Total work ÷ Efficiency of A

⇒ Time taken by A alone = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 days

**∴ The correct answer is 8 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns

This concept is similar to Time & Work. Filling pipes do positive work, while emptying pipes do negative work. Net efficiency = Sum of efficiencies of filling pipes − Sum of efficiencies of emptying pipes.

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in proportion to the total work done by each individual. If workers operate for the same total duration, wages are divided strictly in the ratio of their individual efficiencies.

Alternate Days Work

When workers operate on alternate days, find the total work completed in one full cycle. Then divide the total work by the cycle work to determine the number of completed cycles and any remaining work.
